references.text: Here God loves that Israel should be His own possession and a holy people, the same theme as in Deuteronomy 14:2 about being a holy people and a chosen possession.
Nearly identical text describing Israel as a holy people for the Lord and chosen to be His own possession above all other peoples on earth.
Repeats the promise that Israel is the Lord's own possession and should be a holy people, the same theme as in 14:2.
The psalmist confirms that the Lord has chosen Jacob for Himself and Israel as His own possession.
God speaks of having created and formed Israel, and called them by name as His people.
Paul writes that Christ gave Himself to cleanse a people who belong to Him, a people eager for good works.
Peter describes believers as a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people belonging to God - a direct echo of Deuteronomy 14:2.
